newsitem.title: USA: Consumer groups seek shields in open power market.
newsitem.headline: Consumer groups seek shields in open power market.

text.p: Three big consumer groups Thursday urged Congress to make sure that electricity deregulation does not result in higher residential rates.
In a letter to lawmakers considering legislation to make states open their power markets to competition, the groups said Congress must make sure electricity remains affordable.

"If residential customers are not among the first allowed to benefit from competition, large users will corner the market for lower-priced power," the American Association of Retired Persons, Consumer Federation of America, and Consumers Union said in the letter dated March 13.

Congress should ensure that new institutions that can buy power in bulk for residential customers are tested and in place to bid against industrial power users before deregulating the market, the groups said.
They said utilities should not be allowed to shift all their risks onto consumers as the market opened to competition.
"Utilities should not be compensated for inefficiencies or poor investments, and they should not be compensated excessively for normal business risk," the letter said.
They said transmission, distribution and other costs should be allocated in proportion to use of the facilities.
The groups said social benefits programs, such as the costs of environmental protection and universal service, should be shared among ratepayers, electricity producers and service providers.
To protect residential customers, the groups said legislation should include policies on product information, fair marketing, and billing practices.
